notes.title: DEVLOG - Behind the scenes of Handmancers: how is a character born?
notes.content:
[h3]From initial idea to final execution, here’s a look at the workflow behind character creation in video games, told through the making of one of Handmancers’ iconic enemies: The Living Corpse.[/h3]

[h1]Finding the right balance between gameplay and art direction[/h1]

One of the key elements shaping [i]Handmancers[/i]’ identity, alongside its dynamic gameplay, is the quality of its [b]art direction[/b], which helped build a consistent and recognizable visual world.

Creating a good game isn’t just about [b]strong mechanics[/b]; it’s also about [b]designing characters that stand out and capture the player’s attention[/b], like [i]The Living Corpse[/i], our undead foe.

But how did we bring this character, and all the others, to life. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418950/8e43f0944a9b26232f91e9eb0b77179c71990fa0.png[/img]

[h1]Step 1: concept art. It all starts with the idea.[/h1]

The first step was developing the concept, [b]a character design that felt original while seamlessly fitting the game’s mechanics and overall style[/b].

The Living Corpse is a zombie who, after stealing an [i]Handmancer[/i]’s brain, uses it as an external intelligence, since he has none of his own: it’s the brain that plays, generating a [b]magical hand-shaped aura[/b] to perform moves.

This 2D concept phase is the [b]most creative part of the process[/b], but every proposal goes through team feedback and is adjusted to fit production needs.

We used [b]Procreate[/b] to sketch the first concepts, but pen and paper or other drawing tools would’ve worked just as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418950/da57bfee77bb75c290397e207858a9ee82de86f2.png[/img]

[h1]Step 2: low-poly modeling. The first step into 3D.[/h1]

With the concept locked in, we moved into [b]3D modeling[/b], to give our character [b]depth[/b]. Our first version [b]was built in Maya as a low-poly model[/b], meaning it had a low polygon count.

[b]What does “low-poly” mean?[/b] Polygons are the surface units that make up a 3D model: more polygons means more detail.

At this stage, though, the goal is to create a [b]basic structure[/b] optimized for different platforms (PC and console) before adding complexity later on. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418950/ee19e59f1e7bffa1fdc83841debe7f14b97041cb.png[/img]

[h1]Steps 3 and 4: high-poly modeling & texturing. Adding depth and definition.[/h1]

To transition from a low-poly model to one rich in details, we went through two closely connected phases: [b]high-poly modeling and texturing[/b].

In [b]ZBrush[/b], we added more polygons to the initial model, introducing [b]additional details[/b]. Then in [b]Substance Painter[/b], we used [b]baking[/b] to project these details onto the low-poly model.

[b]What’s baking?[/b] It means capturing the visual details from the high-poly model - such as wrinkles, teeth shapes, and skin texture - and transferring them onto the low-poly version as textures. This creates [b]greater visual fidelity without compromising performance[/b].

Finally, we [b]hand-painted[/b] the model to finalize its look and colors, drawing inspiration from the distinctive [b]visual style of [i]Arcane[/i][/b]: this was the most detailed and time-consuming phase of the entire workflow! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418950/5298f3ec30963e140f29a20efe7011716ca8974d.png[/img]

[h1]Step 5: rigging. Laying the foundation for animation.[/h1]

But the process wasn’t over yet: once the model was complete, it needed to be [b]animated and brought into the game[/b]. The first essential step was [b]rigging[/b], which we handled in Maya.

[b]What is rigging?[/b] Rigging means [b]creating a virtual skeleton made of “bones” that allow the model to move[/b], like a digital puppet. These bones form the control structure used to animate the character.

In essence, rigging defines how a character can move, its range of motion and flexibility: since The Living Corpse is humanoid, we built a [b]skeleton based on the human body[/b]. However, we added extra bones - like in the face and shirt collar - to enhance expressiveness and enable [b]more nuanced animations[/b]. 

[h1]Steps 6 and 7: animation & implementation. Bringing the character to life.[/h1]

The final steps - animating the model and integrating it into the game - were carried out in [b]Unity[/b], the engine we used to develop [i]Handmancers[/i].

Using the skeleton created during rigging, we animated the model [b]by rotating the bones and setting a sequence of keyframes[/b]. These keyframes defined both the movements and their timing, allowing us to craft fluid and intentional animations.

Working directly inside the engine gave us immediate visual feedback, helping us fine-tune the animations quickly and efficiently. 

With visual and sound effects added, the model was nearly ready for the game: we created prefabs, which were implemented alongside ongoing development. This allowed the programmers [b]to align the character’s behavior and logic in real time with the gameplay mechanics of [i]Handmancers[/i][/b].

At last, The Living Corpse was ready to make his debut. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44418950/642b47affaf3de3c0b563541d402092a71c056f7.gif[/img]

[h1]Many characters, a single workflow.[/h1]

Character creation is a careful blend of [b]creativity, artistic skill, and technical execution[/b].

Every character in [i]Handmancers[/i] goes through this same detailed process, helping turn the game into a fully immersive experience.

notes.title: Heartfelt Thank You
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Handmancers![/h1]

[h3]All the team at 58BLADES and I want to thank you all deeply, truly[/h3]
Steam Next Fest was a very exciting time. It was the first time we ever shared Handmancers openly, and let me tell you, we got blown away by [b]your positivity[/b] and [b]feedback[/b] about the game.

[h3]Handmancers was the top35 most played demo of the event[/h3] 
It has now being played by [b]more than 25.000 people[/b] and for more than 51.200 hours (almost 6 years!!!).

[h3]What's next?[/h3]
We are looking forward to take as much as possible of the [b]hundreds of feedbacks[/b] that we received - and are still receiving - into account as we keep developing the game and working towards Early Access!

[b]We care deeply about your opinions, feedback, ideas and suggestions.[/b] Our aim is to keep developing the game with our community throughout the way, making it the best version of Handmancers it can be.

We already uploaded an [b]updated build[/b] with some of the feedback we received, so there might already be something new for you to try if you played the demo during the event.

[h3]Be part of our community![/h3]
If you want to [b]be part of our community[/b] feel free to join our [url=https://discord.gg/3rSHnUTgQq]discord[/url] where we have announcements when something new gets released, or if you just want to [b]share feedback[/b], screenshots or opinions on the game and chat with us developers!

Thank you all, Handmancers.
